policy.sources: A mark ships only when it was retrieved from the source recorded beside it and shipped byte for byte. Nothing here is redrawn, traced, recolored, or reconstructed from a screenshot. Three source kinds appear, and each record says which it is: a vendor's own host, fermix's checked-in plugin catalog, and fermix's own first-party artwork.
policy.no_fabrication: A vendor whose official mark could not be retrieved renders as the vendor text name beside a neutral SF Symbol. A monogram is never invented and another vendor's mark is never substituted.
policy.neutral_symbols: One neutral symbol per roster kind, so the fallback carries no invented vendor identity: providers use cpu, channels use bubble.left.and.bubble.right, meeting platforms use video, plugins and features use puzzlepiece.extension. All exist on the macOS 15 floor.
policy.accessibility: A mark is decorative at every site that draws one: the row around it carries the name, so nothing is spoken twice. The label recorded here is the name that row must speak, and it is unique within its kind. Two kinds may name one vendor, because Discord and Slack are each both a channel and a plugin.
policy.sizing: Marks ship as the vendor's own file, in the format that vendor serves, and the file is named for the format its bytes actually are. An SVG is resolution independent; a raster is at least 128 points on its shorter side, which covers the 20 to 36 point tiles at 2x. A vendor that publishes a horizontal lockup rather than a square icon is shipped as that lockup, because cropping one into a square is an edit no record here permits.
policy.origin: Every record names where its bytes came from, and the refresh step reads it: vendor marks are re-downloaded from the vendor's own URL, while catalog and first_party marks are pinned to fermix's own repository and are re-vendored there rather than fetched from a third party.
policy.plate: Every shipped mark records the plate it is drawn on, and the app reads that field rather than guessing from the pixels. neutral: a coloured glyph on transparency, inset on the app's own tile. bleed: the file is an opaque square or disc carrying its own ground, so it fills the tile and is clipped to its radius. There is deliberately no third plate: a plate painted under a single dark ink is the treatment GitHub and Notion were given on 2026-09-03, and it failed both ways, vanishing into the light ground it matched and glaring on the dark one. A vendor that publishes two inks resolves by appearance, and a vendor that publishes one that already carries its own light ink needs nothing. The catalog's brand_color is not used as a plate either: painting a vendor's brand colour behind a mark authored for white is a recolouring of the mark's context that no record here permits.

marks.usage_terms: The official branding page states the marks may be used to inform people that you are a Discord user or have a Discord server, subject to the brand guidelines, and that you must not edit, change, distort, recolor, or reconfigure the Discord logo, or use the marks on merchandise. marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own symbol files verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolor: the black and white files are the vendor's variants, not tints of the blurple one.
marks.dark_mode_policy: Blurple is the default in both appearances. Where a surface needs a monochrome mark, light appearance takes discord-black and dark appearance takes discord-white, both official files.
marks.notes: The branding page's Color and White symbol download links are transposed relative to the archives they serve: the link labelled Color delivers Discord_Symbol_White and the link labelled White delivers Discord_Symbol_Color. marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own logo files verbatim, scale uniformly, and never render below 26 by 26 points. The wordmark lockups are not used; only the logo glyph is.
marks.dark_mode_policy: Ultramarine is the default in both appearances. Where a surface needs a monochrome mark, light appearance takes signal-black and dark appearance takes signal-white, both official files rather than tints.
marks.notes: The 26 by 26 point floor is the tightest published minimum in this file. Any chip that renders a Signal mark must respect it; the 30 point icon tile in the redlines does.

marks.dark_mode_policy: The kit publishes both inks, so the appearance picks the vendor's own file: black on the light appearance and white on the dark one. Nothing is tinted and no plate is drawn under it.

A plate is what a single dark ink forces, and a plate that matches the light ground is not a plate: on the light appearance it vanished and on the dark one it was the brightest object on the page. Two published inks remove the need for one.

marks.usage_terms: Google's brand resource center routes logo use to its trademark guidelines at https://www.google.com/permissions/trademark/rules/, which state: “Use only Google-approved artwork when using Google’s logos.”, “Maintain clear space around Google logos according to the provided guidelines.”, “Don’t remove, distort, or alter any element of a Google Brand Feature.”, “Don’t display any Google Brand Features as the most prominent element in your content.” and “Don’t display Google Brand Features in any manner that implies a relationship with, affiliation with, sponsorship by, or endorsement by Google.” The brand resource center gates its own asset downloads behind an application (“Please complete your application to access brand resources.”), so what ships is the Google Meet product icon Google itself serves, byte for byte and unmodified.
marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own file verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolored, never cropped, never redrawn. It heads the Google Meet section of the Meetings pane beside that section's name, at the same measure every other mark in settings takes, so it is never the most prominent element on the page, and the copy around it names Google Meet only as a platform the notetaker joins.
marks.dark_mode_policy: One coloured camera glyph on transparency, which reads on both appearances, so it needs no appearance variant, is never rendered as a template image, and is drawn inset on the app's own neutral tile.
marks.notes: meet.google.com references this exact product logo path, which is how the current mark was identified: the older fonts.gstatic.com/s/i/productlogos/meet_2020q4 icon still resolves and is superseded artwork. The raster is taken rather than the 192 point SVG Google serves beside it, for the reason the Google sign-in client already records: AppKit loads that SVG but omits its feGaussianBlur filter, so the soft wedge inside the camera draws with a hard edge. The vendor's own raster renders the complete artwork with no custom renderer.

marks.usage_terms: This is the square application icon Zoom serves for its own site (the touch icon at https://www.zoom.com/apple-touch-icon.png), the current mark since Zoom's rebrand; written guidance is at “Zoom Brand Guidelines”, https://brand.zoom.com/. Zoom's own terms for the marks, published in plain text in its App Marketplace terms of service at https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/legal/zoom-api-license-and-tou/, state: “The “Zoom” word mark and the Zoom logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Zoom (“Zoom Marks”). Subject to compliance with the Terms, Zoom grants SDK App developers a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free, fully paid-up, revocable, worldwide right and license, during the term of use of the Zoom SDK, to use the Zoom Marks solely for display within your SDK App and on your SDK App’s website to promote your SDK App’s compatibility with Zoom’s services and software. Zoom must agree in advance and in writing to all other uses of the Zoom Marks. All uses of the Zoom Marks must comply with Zoom’s Brand Guidelines and Partner Guide, which may be modified from time to time and are available at https://zoom.us/brandguidelines or from brand@zoom.us.” The Brand Center itself is a JavaScript portal: its logo library and the guideline text on it cannot be read without an interactive session, so the terms recorded here are the ones Zoom publishes as text.
marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own file verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolored, never cropped, never re-lettered, never redrawn. It heads the Zoom section of the Meetings pane beside that section's name, and the copy around it names Zoom only as a platform the notetaker joins, never as an endorsement or a partnership.
marks.dark_mode_policy: A white wordmark on Zoom's blue rounded square. The file carries its own ground, so it needs no appearance variant, is never rendered as a template image, and is drawn inset on the app's own neutral tile in both appearances.
marks.notes: Zoom's Brand Center is an interactive portal, so the icon recorded here is the one Zoom serves for its own site chrome: 72 by 72 pixels, which covers the pane's 20 point tile at 2x. The media kit's downloadable file is a horizontal wordmark, which draws as a thin band in a square tile and is not used. The retired camera glyph in a blue circle is not Zoom's current mark and is not an option.
